input.message:
Verified against the live Claude API docs on 2026-10-10. Quotes were checked against raw page copies, saved under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johannesnirschl-Documents-temporary-EHL/40d2eb91-dde3-4e39-8ba4-6686a20b47a7/scratchpad/api-docs/. Sources are listed at the end.

**1. Structured outputs**
- Your shape is the current GA shape: `output_config: { format: { type: "json_schema", schema } }` with `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`. No beta header is needed. The old top-level `output_format` is deprecated and returns 400 unless you send `anthropic-beta: structured-outputs-2025-11-13`.
- `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5` are all listed as supported, GA on the Claude API.
- Allowed: types object/array/string/integer/number/boolean/null; `enum` (string/number/bool/null members only); `const`; `anyOf`; `allOf` (not with `$ref`); `$ref`/`$def`/`definitions` (internal only); `default`; `required`; `additionalProperties: false` on every object; formats date-time, time, date, duration, email, hostname, uri, ipv4, ipv6, uuid; `minItems` of 0 or 1 only; simple regex `pattern`.
- Not allowed (400): recursive schemas; complex enum members; external `$ref`; minimum, maximum, multipleOf; minLength, maxLength; other array constraints; `additionalProperties` other than `false`; regex backreferences, lookaround, `\b`/`\B`, large `{n,m}`.
- Complexity limits: 24 optional parameters, 16 union-typed parameters (`anyOf` or type arrays), 180 s compile timeout.
- Enum values may come back with different capitalization. Required properties are emitted first.
- Incompatible with citations and assistant prefill.

**2. Thinking and effort (5.5 models)**
- Use `thinking: { type: "adaptive" }` (or omit `thinking`, which is adaptive by default) plus `output_config: { effort }`. `effort` accepts low, medium, high, xhigh, max on all three. `"adaptive"` is not an effort value.
- Effort defaults: Opus 5.5 = medium, Sonnet 5.5 = high, Haiku 5.5 = medium. Set `high` explicitly if you want it.
- `thinking: { type: "enabled", budget_tokens }` returns 400 on all three. There is no `budget_tokens` on these models.
- Turning thinking off:
  - Opus 5.5: always on. `disabled` returns 400 at every effort level.
  - Sonnet 5.5: `disabled` returns 400. Use `{ type: "between_tools" }`, which works at low, medium and high and returns 400 at xhigh and max.
  - Haiku 5.5: `{ type: "disabled" }` works at high or below and returns 400 at xhigh and max.
- Thinking plus `output_config.format`: the docs list no incompatibility. The grammar applies only to the final text, not to thinking. No doc page shows `effort` and `format` in the same `output_config`, although the schema allows both. Verify with one live call.
- With thinking on:
  - Do not send `temperature`, `top_p` or `top_k`. Non-default values return 400. `top_p: 1` returns 400 because the default is 0.99. Sending both `temperature` and `top_p` returns 400, even at their defaults.
  - There is no budget relationship. `max_tokens` is one hard cap on thinking plus text combined.
  - `tool_choice` of `any` or `tool` returns 400 on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. Haiku 5.5 is not on that list.
  - Prefilling the final assistant turn returns 400 on 4.6-generation and later models. Use `output_config.format` instead.

**3. Response shape and stop reasons**
- Content block types: `{ type: "thinking", thinking: string, signature: string }`, `{ type: "redacted_thinking", data: string }`, `{ type: "text", text: string }`. Thinking blocks come before text blocks.
- On these models, `display` defaults to `"omitted"`. The `thinking` field is then `""`, but `signature` is still present. `thinking: { type: "adaptive", display: "summarized" }` returns a summary, not the raw chain of thought. You are billed for the full thinking either way.
- Get the JSON from the text block (`content.find(b => b.type === "text")`), never from `content[0]`.
- Thinking blocks from Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 work only in the account that produced them. If you replay turns, pass blocks back unchanged.
- `stop_reason` values (seven):
  - `end_turn`: complete.
  - `max_tokens`: incomplete. Output may be truncated or missing its text block, because thinking counts toward the limit.
  - `model_context_window_exceeded`: treat as truncated.
  - `refusal`: the JSON may not match the schema. `stop_details` is `{ type, category, explanation }`. It arrives as HTTP 200 and is billed, so check `stop_reason`, not only the status code.
  - `stop_sequence`: only if you set `stop_sequences`. Treat as incomplete for JSON, which is my inference.
  - `tool_use`: no final JSON. Only occurs when you pass tools.
  - `pause_turn`: server-tool loop limit. Not final; resend as-is.
- Only `end_turn` is complete.
- `usage`: `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` (includes thinking; the billing total), `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation: { ephemeral_5m_input_tokens, ephemeral_1h_input_tokens }`, and `output_tokens_details: { thinking_tokens }`, a breakdown only. Total input = `input_tokens` + `cache_creation_input_tokens` + `cache_read_input_tokens`.

**4. Max output tokens**
- Synchronous limit is 128K (128,000) for all three. Batches allow 300K with `output-300k-2026-03-24`.
- No doc gives a number for high effort. Doc examples for thinking use `max_tokens: 16000`. The documented starting point at xhigh or max on Opus 5 is 64k. Sonnet 5.5 agentic coding uses 128,000. My suggestion is 16,000 for JSON-only output at high effort, raised if you see `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`.
- The official SDK requires streaming above `max_tokens` 21,333. The docs advise streaming or Batches for requests over 10 minutes. A raw fetch client has no such check, but idle connections can drop.

**5. Errors and retries**
- Error body: `{ "type": "error", "error": { "type", "message" }, "request_id": "req_..." }`. The response header is `request-id`.
- `error.type` values: `invalid_request_error` (400), `authentication_error` (401), `billing_error` (402), `permission_error` (403), `not_found_error` (404), `conflict_error` (409), `request_too_large` (413), `rate_limit_error` (429), `api_error` (500), `timeout_error` (504), `overloaded_error` (529). The docs say this list may grow, so do not hard-fail on unknown types.
- Retry:
  - 429: wait `retry-after` seconds. A monthly spend-cap 429 has no `retry-after` and keeps failing until access resumes.
  - 500: exponential backoff.
  - 529: no explicit rule in the docs. Treat it as a transient 5xx.
  - 409: the docs say to resolve the conflict, then retry.
  - 504: the docs recommend streaming for long requests and give no retry rule.
- Do not retry 400, 401, 402, 403, 404 or 413.
- The official SDKs retry connection errors, 429 and 5xx with exponential backoff, twice by default, honoring `retry-after`.

**6. Prompt caching**
- Placement:
  ```json
  "system": [
    { "type": "text", "text": "...static instructions...", "cache_control": { "type": "ephemeral" } }
  ]
  ```
  Put the breakpoint on the last static block. You can define up to 4 breakpoints per request.
- Minimum cacheable length: 512 tokens for all three on the Claude API, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS. Bedrock has its own minimums. Shorter prompts are silently not cached. If `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` are both 0, the prompt was not cached.
- TTL: the default is 5 minutes, refreshed on each hit. For 1 hour, use `{ "type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h" }`, at extra cost. No beta header is needed.
- Invalidation: changing `output_config.format` invalidates the cache for that thread. Changing the thinking config or effort invalidates cached message blocks.

**7. Model IDs**
- Valid API IDs: `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`. The same strings work on Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS. Bedrock uses `anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` and so on.
- No dated IDs exist for these models. Dateless IDs from the 4.6 generation on are pinned snapshots, not floating aliases. The "alias" row in the docs repeats the same string.
- Context window is 1M tokens. Retirement is not sooner than Sep 22, 2027 (Opus 5.5), Sep 28, 2027 (Sonnet 5.5) and Oct 7, 2027 (Haiku 5.5).

**Minimal request body (combines your current shape with adaptive thinking and effort)**
```json
{
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
  "max_tokens": 16000,
  "thinking": { "type": "adaptive" },
  "output_config": {
    "effort": "high",
    "format": { "type": "json_schema", "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "name": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["name"], "additionalProperties": false } }
  },
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "..." }]
}
```
Parsing: throw unless `stop_reason === "end_turn"`, take the `type === "text"` block, `JSON.parse` it, then validate against your schema. The docs say structured outputs guarantee compliance only "in most cases".

**Caveats**
- The `effort` plus `format` combination is schema-valid but unshown in the docs. Test it once.
- Do not ask for step-by-step reasoning inside a JSON field. That can trigger a `reasoning_extraction` refusal.

**Sources**
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-troubleshooting
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-steering-and-cost
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/handling-stop-reasons
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/create
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/versioning
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta-headers
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/model-ids-and-versions
